reading: Four 3x3 shapes lie scattered on the grid; the output is a 7x7 grid that packs them into a 2x2 layout (one empty row and column between) keeping their relative positions: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

slots.pieces: the four 3x3 single-colour objects (cropped to their 3x3 boxes)
slots.layout: 2x2 slots of 3x3 with a 1-cell background gap, output 7x7
slots.order: slot chosen by the object's relative position (upper/lower, left/right)

why: each output 3x3 slot equals the 3x3 box of the input object in that quadrant

reading: A colour-1 wall sits at the top with notches on its underside; each colour-5 piece below that (in some rotation or reflection) could plug one underside notch completely, with any extra cells hanging out below, is recoloured 2; other pieces stay 5.

slots.lock: the colour-1 object; its notches are the background pockets inside its row span that open downward only
slots.test: piece, rotated/reflected and translated, covers a whole notch, overlaps no 1-cell, and its other cells lie below the wall

why: exactly the 5-pieces that can plug some underside notch become 2; nothing else changes

reading: Single coloured cells move to touch the nearest grey 2x2 block, landing on the nearest free cell adjacent (8-neighbour) to it; the grey blocks stay put.

new_rows.name: singles
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
singles(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 1.

why: every single cell ends 8-adjacent to a grey block at the nearest free contact cell (a closer cell claims a contested spot first)

reading: Two coloured cells, one in the top half and one in the bottom half; the output draws a frame: the top half (rows 0-4) in the upper cell's colour with the outer top row and the cell's row filled full and side columns filled; the bottom half (rows 5-9) likewise in the lower cell's colour with its row and the bottom row full.

slots.upper half: rows 0..H/2-1 in upper colour: border row 0, left/right border columns, full line on the seed's row
slots.lower half: rows H/2..H-1 in lower colour: border row H-1, left/right border columns, full line on the seed's row

why: every output cell is the colour of the seed of its half if it lies on the grid border or on that seed's row, else background

reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block: each of its 8 outer cells shoots a ray in its own direction away from the centre (edges straight, corners diagonal) in its own colour until the grid border; the centre stays.
why: every ray runs from an outer block cell outward along its direction from the block centre to the border, in that cell's colour

reading: The grid is cut into 3x3 panels by separator lines; the top-left panel holds the template shape. In every panel, template positions that are background are filled with the separator colour; existing cells keep their colour.

slots.template: non-background cells of the top-left panel
slots.panels: cells cut by the full separator lines

why: in every panel, each template position is non-background in the output; cells off the template are unchanged

reading: Each L-tromino casts a diagonally shifted copy of itself into background cells: grey (5) Ls get a colour-4 copy shifted one step toward the missing corner of their 2x2 box; red (2) Ls get a colour-3 copy shifted one step away from it (3 overrides 4 where they meet).

slots.offset: diagonal unit step toward (5) or away from (2) the empty corner of the object's 2x2 box
slots.rest: copies only fill background; originals kept

why: every changed cell is a background cell covered by the diagonal copy of an adjacent L, coloured by the L's colour

reading: A 2x2 block contains some red (2) cells; the block is swept diagonally to the grid border in the direction of each red corner, the whole swept band painted in the block's non-red colour.

slots.subject: the 2x2 block
slots.directions: for each red cell, the diagonal pointing from the block centre through that cell
slots.colour: the block's non-red colour (also repaints the block)

why: the output is the union of the block and all its diagonal translates along each red-corner direction, in one colour

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled by 2: each grey cell becomes the 2x2 tile [[1,2],[2,1]] and each background cell a 2x2 background tile.
why: output block (i,j) is the fixed tile when input cell (i,j) is non-background, else empty

reading: The top band is a legend: three 3x3 colour blocks with a marker colour under each. Below the separator row, the output is that lower panel with each marker replaced by a 3x3 block (centred on it) of the colour its marker colour is paired with in the legend.

slots.legend: top panel: 3x3 block colour paired with the single marker cell beneath it
slots.canvas: the panel below the full separator row (output size)
slots.unit: 3x3 block centred on the anchor, colour = legend(marker colour)

why: output = lower panel background with one 3x3 legend-coloured block centred on every marker
